subject: Advance prepay structure, invoicing entity & tax handling for NordicHealth
messages:
From: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordichealth.se>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:14:00 +0100
Subject: Redwood prepay options & invoicing entity question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput profile and the enterprise controls. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few practical questions before we move to commercial redlines:

- We plan to prepay credits across a multi‑year commitment (thinking 3 years). Can you confirm the term discounts you offer for 2yr vs 3yr prepay commitments and whether those discounts apply to both committed units and baseline overage rates?
- NordicHealth prefers to pay in EUR and to have invoices from your EU entity to avoid FX volatility. Do you have an EU invoicing option (entity, VAT registration)? If invoiced from the US entity, will Redwood charge VAT? If not, what do you need from us to trigger reverse charge?
- Our treasury requires clarity on withholding tax (WHT). For payments routed from Sweden to the vendor, are we expected to withhold any taxes? If so, can Redwood accept net-of-WHT pricing or do you require a gross-up clause?
- One more: we want a ramp schedule (year 1 smaller, year 2 ramp, year 3 full utilization). Can you confirm how unused prepay is treated and whether we can reallocate across EU regions?

We’ll also need a sample invoice and a term sheet to show to tax/finance. Can you send a short term sheet and sample invoice?

Best,
Anna Svensson
Head of Procurement, NordicHealth AB
anna.svensson@nordichealth.se

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Redwood prepay options & invoicing entity question

Hi Anna — great to hear the demo resonated. Quick answers and next steps below; looping finance and legal to confirm the tax language.

1) Term discounts: we can offer a sliding discount on committed prepaid units: 2‑year = 12% off list, 3‑year = 20% off list. These discounts apply to the committed bucket. For overage pricing we can either: (a) keep overage at standard list rates, or (b) offer a discounted overage tied to commitment (we typically offer 10% off overage if you commit to a 3yr ramp schedule). Let me know which you prefer.

2) Invoicing entity & VAT: we have an EU entity that can invoice in EUR (preferred for EU customers). If you provide a valid EU VAT ID we can issue invoices net of VAT under reverse charge. If invoiced from the US entity and you do not provide VAT ID, local VAT may be charged. Marcus (cc) will confirm the exact paperwork.

3) Withholding tax: our standard is to invoice gross and not expect withholdings. We can accept net-of‑WHT with a contractual gross‑up or a negotiated WHT credit. Laura (legal) — can we propose the gross‑up language for procurement?

4) Ramp & reallocations: yes — we can structure a three‑year ramp (you specify committed units per year: e.g., 50%/75%/100%). Unused committed units in a year can be reallocated within the same legal entity/region subject to a quarterly reconciliation; we will document a small carry‑forward allowance and an annual true‑up.

Attached: Redwood_PrePay_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf — high level: pricing bands, proposed discounts, and sample ramp schedule. Also sharing a sample invoice from our EU entity in EUR.

Propose a short call tomorrow to align on which of the overage options you prefer and to confirm invoicing entity.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Clarification: VAT, WHT and EUR invoicing options

Hi Anna/Rachel — Marcus from Finance here. A few clarifications to help your tax team:

- VAT: For B2B services within the EU, we can issue invoices net of VAT under the reverse charge mechanism provided we receive a valid EU VAT number for the billing entity. If the customer does not provide a VAT ID, we are required to charge VAT at the local rate.
- Invoicing entity: We have a Redwood EMEA (Ireland) entity that can invoice in EUR. Invoicing from the Ireland entity avoids USD->EUR FX for you, but note there is sometimes a small FX/settlement admin margin applied when converting internal accounting — we typically bake this into the offer rather than a separate fee.
- WHT: Sweden does not generally levy WHT on pure software/service fees paid to non‑resident vendors. However, certain jurisdictions do. If NordicHealth expects to withhold tax, our commercial options are: (1) Gross‑up: Redwood invoices the gross amount and customer reimburses any WHT deducted; (2) Net pricing: we discount the gross price by an agreed WHT estimate and include a true‑up clause. 
- Sample invoice: attached a stubbed EUR invoice to show fields we include (VAT ID, invoice number, bank details).

If you can share your VAT ID and the billing legal entity, I can prepare an invoice example with final totals (EUR) for the proposed 3yr structure.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: Sample_EUR_Invoice_stub.pdf (8KB)

Thanks Rachel/Marcus — quick internal update: procurement and treasury are aligned to proceed with a 3‑year prepay if the following are confirmed in writing:

- Pricing: 3yr committed discount applied to committed units (we favour the 20% band you suggested) and a 10% discounted overage rate for customers on the 3yr program.
- Ramp schedule: propose Year1 50% of forecasted consumption, Year2 75%, Year3 100% (we'll provide a quarterly forecast). Unused committed units can be reallocated across our EU subsidiaries.
- Invoicing: prefer invoices from Redwood EMEA (Ireland) in EUR and will provide VAT ID — confirm that no VAT will be charged under reverse charge.
- WHT: treasury requires a clause that NordicHealth will not be liable for additional gross‑up payments beyond the agreed pricing—we will provide local confirmation (Sweden) that WHT is 0% for these services, but need contractual language in the event of any unexpected deduction.

Can you send an updated term sheet and a redlineable SOW (DocuSign option preferred)? Also confirm whether the 3yr discount will be price‑protected for the contract term (no mid‑term CPI or license fee increases).

Regards,
Anna Svensson
Head of Procurement, NordicHealth AB

Subject: Re: Advance prepay structure, invoicing entity & tax handling for NordicHealth (contract language)

Hi Anna — Laura from Legal. Thanks for the clarity on the commercial points. A couple of legal clarifications/proposals so procurement can review: 

1) WHT / gross-up: we can include a clause that states: "Customer shall make payments without deduction for or on account of any taxes, levies or withholdings. If Customer is legally required to withhold or deduct any such amounts, Customer shall (a) notify Redwood promptly and (b) pay to Redwood an additional amount such that Redwood receives the net amount it would have received had no deduction been made." This preserves commercial certainty. If NordicHealth has statutory confirmation (0% WHT) we can add a carve‑out.

2) Price protection: we can guarantee the committed unit pricing (including the 3yr discount) for the contract term. We reserve a CPI‑linked adjustment for certain pass‑through costs beyond 12 months, but we can make that explicit and limited (e.g., CPI adjustments only on support services, not token unit pricing).

3) Ramp & carryforward: propose a quarterly reconciliation and a 10% annual carryforward pool for unused committed units; any remaining excess will be converted to overage at the agreed overage rate.

I'll prepare a redlineable SOW and updated term sheet that reflect the above. If these points are acceptable I can send DocuSign-ready documents for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
